key_insight: A digital quantum computer can faithfully simulate real-time string dynamics in a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model by encoding dual height variables into qubits and matching the lattice to hardware connectivity.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a practical route for studying confining gauge theories and non-equilibrium dynamics on near-term quantum hardware where classical Monte Carlo methods fail.
method: Mapped the U(1) quantum link model to qubit dual height variables for efficient plaquette interactions.
Used a lattice geometry tailored to IBM heavy-hex hardware to reduce non-adjacent qubit couplings.
Ran quantum quenches from a simple string state to probe transverse fluctuations and thermalization.
evidence_signal: Experiments on up to 112 qubits agreed with tensor-network benchmarks at short times and thermal averages at long times, with error-mitigated results remaining accurate even near the phase transition.
watch_item: Results depend on hardware-specific geometry and error mitigation, and gauge-symmetry violations still arise from noise and finite-depth/finite-bond-dimension effects.
paper_title: String dynamics of a (2+1)D U(1) quantum link model on a digital quantum computer
